subject: Request: Temporary activation-window penalty exemption for multi-region failover
messages:
From: Asha Patel <asha.patel@finlogix.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@finlogix.com
Date: Sat, 4 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: activation window carveout for warm-standby activation

Hi Camila,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We ran the resilience simulation with our infra team and a few constraints came up that are causing us to request a short-term carveout to Redwood's standard multi-region failover obligations.

Summary of ask: FinLogix needs a 6-month limited exemption from the automatic SLA penalty clause tied to warm-standby activation lead time for the secondary region. Specifically, for cross-region warm-to-hot switchover initiated by our platform, we need the activation lead time SLO extended from 15 minutes to 45 minutes for up to three planned activations per month while we complete on-prem data-migration work and DR runbooks. We are not asking to change RTO/RPO target ceilings permanently — just the penalty assessment for those activations while our migration project is underway.

Why: We're moving sensitive reconciliation workloads into a dedicated VPC that requires additional preflight checks (data sync verification with HSM-backed key rotation). That process adds ~20–30 minutes to safe activation.

Risk mitigations we propose:
- Canary window: first activation each month will be performed during a guarded maintenance window (Redwood ops + FinLogix oncall).
- KV-prefix caching to minimize token re-warm time
- Read-only replication testing before each activation
- Post-activation playbook and runbook share (we can supply the runbook and evidence after each activation)

Attached is the short request packet and our migration timeline. Can Redwood provide a way to document this as a limited SLA addendum (term-limited, tied to the migration project) rather than forcing a redline to the base SLA?

Appreciate your thoughts — happy to set up a 30m sync next week.

Best,
Asha
Head of Platform Engineering
FinLogix

Attachments: FinLogix_SLA_Request.pdf (2 pages)

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Asha Patel <asha.patel@finlogix.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Aug 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: activation window carveout for warm-standby activation

Hi Asha — thanks for the clear request and the attached packet. We can absolutely discuss a time-limited addendum; we often handle similar asks with an SLA addendum that scopes the carveout (dates, max activations, mitigation controls) and preserves the overall RTO/RPO commitments outside of the specified activations.

Initial thoughts:
- We can accept a 6-month addendum if the mitigation controls you listed are enforced programmatically (evidence via weekly post-activation reports and a shared runbook).
- We will require a canary engagement for the first activation each month with Redwood oncall present and a joint sign-off.
- We may propose a reduced penalty rather than a full exemption: e.g., 50% penalty reduction for covered activations, instead of zeroing penalties. That preserves economic alignment while acknowledging migration constraints.

I'll loop in Marissa (contracts) and Karthik (technical SRE) to comment on contract language and the operational checklist. Can you propose two slots next week for a 30m call? We'll draft a slim addendum and share before the call (attachment: Redwood_SLA_Addendum_v1.docx).

—Camila
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Camila Reyes | camila_reyes@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0183

Camila / Karthik — quick internal notes before we speak to FinLogix:

1) Contract/legal: the addendum approach is fine but we should avoid language that creates a precedent of full penalty waivers. Suggested framing: "Temporary Operational Exception — Limited Penalty Relief". Limit to 6 months with an automatic expiry. Require written evidence and retention (S3 link) for each activation.

2) Operational gating: Karthik, we need a short checklist that teams can validate before allowing the extended activation window to be considered "covered" by the addendum:
   - Runbook uploaded and verified (signed by FinLogix ops lead)
   - Pre-switchover data sync verification (hash checks)
   - Joint oncall presence during first activation of each month
   - Post-activation telemetry snapshot (latency, error rates, token counts)

3) Escalation & rollback: If post-activation telemetry shows >0.5% error increase for 30m, the event is considered a failed activation and normal penalties apply. We should include a clause to allow Redwood to revert to standard SLA early if migration causes operational instability.

4) Finance: Logan, please estimate the expected revenue at risk for six months and compute a blended penalty exposure if we did 3 activations/month with 50% penalty reduction. We need this number before legal signs off.

I'll be on the FinLogix call on Thursday at 10:00 PST. Camila, can you confirm the calendar invite?

—Marissa
Director, Contracts & Renewals
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Request: activation window carveout for warm-standby activation

Hi Asha — great to sync yesterday. Thanks for walking us through the migration milestones. Per that call, attached is Redwood_SLA_Addendum_v1 (we updated the gating checklist and penalty language). Key points in short:

- Term: Aug 15, 2028 — Feb 14, 2029 (6 months)
- Covered activations: up to 3 planned warm->hot activations per calendar month; ad-hoc emergency activations are excluded
- Penalty treatment: covered activations receive a 50% reduction to the standard activation lead-time penalty; standard penalties apply otherwise
- Operational gates: runbook upload, pre-switchover hash verification, joint oncall for the first activation each month, and post-activation telemetry snapshot uploaded to the shared S3 path within 24 hours
- Failure clause: if any covered activation causes >0.5% sustained error-rate increase for 30 minutes, Redwood may revoke the addendum early with 7 days' notice

Next steps for FinLogix: please: (1) confirm acceptance of the addendum as drafted, (2) provide the runbook S3 path for evidence uploads, and (3) confirm the first planned activation date so we can schedule the canary with ops. Once you confirm, Contracts will route the addendum for signature (DocuSign).

Thanks — looking forward to keeping this low-friction while protecting both sides.

—Camila
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_SLA_Addendum_v1.docx; link to DocuSign route once countersigned.
